page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The server configuration allocates 24 dedicated vCPUs spanning 12 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, supported by 35 MB of shared L3 cache and hardware extensions including AVX-512 and AES. Memory capacity is provisioned at 24.0 GB, resulting in a strict 1:1 gigabyte-to-vCPU allocation. The instance features no bundled local storage and connects through an 8 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark evaluations reflect a distinct division between single-threaded and parallel processing. Single-core performance falls in the lower tiers, as demonstrated by weak outcomes in stress-ng single-core (1107.99), Geekbench single-core (1009.0), and single-threaded gzip compression. When multi-threading is applied, the 24 dedicated cores deliver mid-tier aggregate output, producing a PassMark CPU score of 18361.58, a Geekbench multi-core score of 7777.0, and 17.02 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Memory throughput tests show lower tier responsiveness on PassMark memory benchmarks, aligning with the dense CPU-to-memory configuration.

The primary technical tradeoff of this instance is its constrained RAM allocation relative to its high core count. With only 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, memory-intensive applications face memory starvation unless scaled carefully. Cost efficiency is achieved when running high-concurrency, CPU-bound tasks that do not require expansive memory buffers or fast local storage drives. The instance is structured for distributed compilation, multi-threaded batch data transformations, image rendering, and static web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor on the KVM hypervisor. Featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores with hyperthreading and 35 MB of L3 cache, the system is configured with 24.0 GB of RAM, yielding an aggressive 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes no local storage and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network throughput. In benchmark tests, single-thread performance is modest, while parallel processing achieves solid mid-tier output across multi-core Geekbench, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded decompression tests. The constrained memory allocation limits its utility for memory-heavy databases or caching layers, but its dedicated compute density delivers cost-efficient multi-threaded compute. The ecs.ic5.6xlarge is well fitted for distributed compilation tasks, multi-threaded batch processing, parallel rendering jobs, and front-end web serving with low memory footprints.
